claims.text: Greg LaVecchia (founder of Bloom Nutrition) asserts that the primary value of private jet travel is eliminating the airport experience entirely, which removes hours from total travel time, not the in-flight amenities or cabin experience. A second distinct benefit is full control over departure and landing timing.
claims.speaker: Greg LaVecchia
claims.mechanism: Skipping commercial airport check-in, security, boarding, and gate processes removes the largest time sinks in air travel; time savings accrue from process elimination, not speed-of-flight improvement.
bounded_by: In-flight amenities on small private jets (e.g., Citation CJ2, 6-seat) are minimal compared to commercial premium cabin; the value is purely time-cost removal, not comfort superiority

examples.text: Greg LaVecchia documented a private jet trip in a YouTube Short (50 seconds, 2024): traveling on a Citation CJ2 with two others (a camera operator and Leo, President of Bloom Nutrition), they drove directly to the plane and boarded without any airport processing. He noted the jet was technically a six-seater but they prefer flying with three to four people. The bathroom is minimal (toilet only). His conclusion: the singular advantage is bypassing the airport entirely, which saves hours, plus the ability to set your own departure and arrival times.

practices.text: When communicating the value of a premium time-saving product or service to a wealthy audience, lead with time removal (hours saved, process eliminated) rather than luxury features or in-product amenities.
